oligos.sugar_modifications: 2'-F pyrimidines and 2'-OH (unmodified ribose) purines, per Figure 2 caption: 'The pyrimidines in the aptamer are modified with 2'F-nucleotides while the purines are composed of 2'OH-nucleotides.'
oligos.conjugate: 5' cholesterol; 3' end blocked by an inverted deoxythymidine (idT). Figure 2 caption: 'The 5'-end of the aptamer contains a cholesterol, and the 3'-end is blocked by an idT.'
oligos.notes: CHEMISTRY DIFFERS FROM RB006/pegnivacogin in the same drug family: this source states 2'-OH (unmodified) purines, whereas the S27 key-resource table prints a 2'-OMe/2'-F case convention for RB006. Do not merge the two chemistries. DOSE CONTRADICTION INSIDE THIS SOURCE: Abstract and Methods both state 10 mg/kg ('the other group received 10 mg/kg of the cholesterol-modified version of the FIXa aptamer'), but the Discussion states 'in this experiment, the FIXa aptamer dose was 5 mg/kg, which was 10-fold higher than that used in the porcine bypass experiments'. All measurement rows below carry the Methods/Figure-3 dose of 10 mg/kg because that is the dose printed in the figure legend that the numbers come from; the 5 mg/kg statement is unreconciled.

oligos.notes: THE TRIAGE SHEET SAID 'sequences: no' FOR THIS SOURCE; that is wrong - the KEY RESOURCE TABLE publishes the full sequence for both RB006 and RB005 WITH an explicit per-position case legend, which is why the modifications array is populated for this bundle. HAZARD FOR THE REVIEWER: applying the printed legend literally assigns 2'-F to purines (A and G appear in upper case at positions 3,4,5,8,10,13,15,17,18,20 and 23 is the parenthesised unmodified G), which is unusual for this aptamer class - published anti-FIXa aptamer chemistry is normally 2'-F pyrimidine. Every lower-case character in the printed string is a pyrimidine (c or u). The modifications array below follows the printed legend EXACTLY and does not correct it; it should be checked against Dyke et al. 2006 before use. Also: 6 of 18 healthy rhesus monkeys developed significant anti-PEG IgG after a SINGLE administration of RB006 (Figure 6, Table 1) - an immunogenicity finding, not a coagulation readout, so no measurement row was written for it.

oligos.target_gene: TFPI (protein target: tissue factor pathway inhibitor)
oligos.developer: Archemix Corp. (Cambridge, MA) - 'BAX499 was provided by Archemix Corp.'; grant support to the authors from Archemix
oligos.max_phase: NOT_REPORTED in this source (in vitro / ex vivo only)

oligos.conjugate: PEGylated - 'we evaluate BAX499, a polyethylene glycol conjugated aptamer that specifically binds to TFPI' (Introduction). PEG size not stated.
oligos.notes: OPPOSITE SIGN COMPOUND: engineered to be PROCOAGULANT (TFPI antagonist). on_target_effect is true on rows where thrombin generation rises or clot time shortens. The source itself documents an on-target-vs-observed divergence: (a) the calculated apparent Kd for the BAX499/TFPI interaction RISES with increasing aptamer concentration (1.2-1.8 nM at 2.5-25 nM, 5.8 nM at 100 nM, 11.8 nM at 250 nM), which the authors attribute to the TFPI-aptamer complex itself retaining FXa-inhibitory activity; (b) saturating BAX499 restores only 75-80% of extrinsic FXase activity; (c) in whole blood the aptamer repairs clot time but does NOT restore the propagation phase, and in 2 of 3 TEG subjects the clots formed with BAX499 lysed FASTER than without it. NOTE ON A CLAIM I DID NOT FIND: the triage sheet describes a 'paradoxical plasma TFPI rise' and programme discontinuation for BAX499. Neither appears anywhere in this source or in the sibling abstracts file, so no row asserts it.

measurements.verbatim_quote: In the absence of BAX499, TFPI decreased the concentration of active FXa from 1 nM at zero time to 0.19 nM after 15 minutes (Figure 1A). Analysis of this binding isotherm indicated that the Kd for TFPI and FXa was ~0.4 nM, consistent with a previous report [39]. With increasing BAX499, the effect of TFPI was lessened in a concentration dependent manner. At 250 nM aptamer, 0.76 nM FXa remained after 15 minutes.
measurements.notes: Intermediate aptamer concentrations (2.5, 5, 10, 25, 100 nM) are plotted in Figure 1A only and were NOT read off the image. BAX499 is a PROCOAGULANT (TFPI-antagonist) aptamer, so on_target_effect true with a shortening/increasing direction is the intended pharmacology, not a toxicity.

measurements.verbatim_quote: Between 2.5 and 25 nM BAX499, the calculated Kd ranged between 1.2 and 1.8 nM. However, the calculated Kd increased at higher aptamer concentrations. At 100 nM aptamer, the calculated Kd was 5.8 nM. At 250 nM aptamer, the calculated Kd increased to 11.8 nM.
measurements.notes: ON-TARGET-VS-OBSERVED DIVERGENCE ROW. unintended_toxicity is set FALSE deliberately: this is an unintended paradoxical pharmacology (loss of apparent potency at high concentration), not a toxicity. The authors excluded aggregation ('light scattering measurements with up to 1.5 μM BAX499 showed no evidence of aggregation') and propose instead that 'the TFPI-aptamer complex is itself an inhibitor of fXa, but with lower affinity'. This is the mechanistic seed of the drug's known clinical problem and should be carried forward as such.

extraction_notes:
SCOPE. Bundle 'aptamers-invivo': aptamer in-vivo and reversal/antidote studies, plus the anti-PEG interference mechanism and the procoagulant outlier BAX499. Six source records, seven distinct oligonucleotide entities, both sign directions of the coagulopathy endpoint.

1. AN EXTRA SOURCE KEY WAS CREATED: S31b. The bundle sheet numbers five ranks (S26, S27, S29, S30, S31) but the triage notes for S30 and S31 both designate the sibling PubMed file pubmed_REG1_pegnivacogin_BAX499_abstracts.txt as separately extractable ("each is a separate extractable row"). Those rows are filed under a sixth source entry, source_key "S31b", so they never masquerade as S31 full-text data. Every S31b row names its own PMID and journal in source_locus. S31b is NOT a bundle rank; downstream joins keyed strictly on S<integer> must be told about it. PMID 18506005 appears in that file as record 5 and is ALSO S31; it was extracted once, under S31, not twice.

2. THE TRIAGE SHEET SAID "sequences: no" FOR S27. THAT IS WRONG AND IT IS THE MOST VALUABLE FINDING IN THIS BUNDLE. The S27 KEY RESOURCE TABLE prints full sequences for RB006 (pegnivacogin) and RB005 with an explicit per-position case legend: "40 kDa mPEG-GUGGAcuAuAccGcGuAAuGcU(G)CcuCCACidT: (uppercase-2' F, lowercase-2'O Methyl, ()-unmodified)". That is the only per-position chemistry legend in this bundle, so the modifications array is populated for exactly those two oligos (31 positions each, 62 rows) and is empty for everything else. Position 31 is the 3' inverted dT; counting it reproduces the "31 nucleotide" length the S27 Methods state, which is the internal check that the reading is right.

3. HAZARD ON THAT SEQUENCE - READ BEFORE USING THE MODIFICATIONS ARRAY. Applied literally, the printed legend assigns 2'-F to purines: upper-case A and G occur at positions 3,4,5,8,10,13,15,17,18,20 and the only parenthesised (unmodified) base is the G at position 23. Every lower-case character in the string is a pyrimidine. Published anti-FIXa aptamer chemistry in this lineage is normally 2'-F pyrimidine, so the case convention as printed in this Key Resource Table may be inverted or garbled. I followed the printed legend EXACTLY and corrected nothing; the basis field on every modification row states which rule produced it. Verify against Dyke et al. 2006 before any structure-activity use.

4. LICENCE CONTRADICTION INSIDE S26, CARRIED AS THE STRICTER READING. The PMC <permissions> block of PMC12208382 contains BOTH a machine-readable ali:license_ref pointing at https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/ (content-type "ccbysalicense") AND printed licence prose reading "Creative Commons Attribution-Non Commercial-No Derivatives License 4.0 (CCBY-NC-ND) ... The work cannot be changed in any way or used commercially without permission from the journal." These are incompatible (BY-SA permits commercial use and derivatives; BY-NC-ND forbids both). Recorded as CC_BY_NC_ND.

5. INTERNAL CONTRADICTIONS FOUND, NONE SILENTLY RESOLVED.
   (a) S26 DOSE: Abstract and Methods say the aptamer dose was 10 mg/kg; the Discussion says "in this experiment, the FIXa aptamer dose was 5 mg/kg". Rows carry 10 mg/kg because that is the dose printed in the Figure 3 legend the numbers come from. Flagged on the oligo record and on the rows.
   (b) S26 READOUT LABEL: the post-reversal values "60 ± 13 seconds and 79 ± 28 seconds" are called ACT but appear inside the paragraph explicitly about aPTT, and they contradict the ACT post-antidote value of 130 s given one paragraph earlier for the same animals at the same timepoint. That row's readout_name is written "ACT_or_aPTT_UNRESOLVED" rather than being quietly reassigned.
   (c) S29 BASELINES: three of six baseline medians/ranges in the running text do not reconcile with Table 1 day-1 values (platelets, VWF:GpIbM, VWF:RCo); three do (FVIII, VWF:Ag, VWF:CB). Also day 0 vs day 1 dosing-day inconsistency between Methods/Results and the Abstract/Figure 2 caption. Detailed on each per-patient row.
   (d) S31b PMID 18284597 prints "intraclass correlation coefficient 5.8", which is out of range for an ICC. Recorded verbatim, not rescaled.

6. CENSORED VALUES - FOUR OF THEM, ALL FLAGGED IN ROW NOTES. (i) S26: heparin-arm aPTT exceeded the assay ceiling and was recorded as 500 s with no error bars at 5 and 30 min, so every aptamer-vs-heparin aPTT comparison is against a censored comparator; the aptamer arm itself stayed on scale. (ii) S30: the TFPI-only extrinsic-FXase rate is left-censored below the detection limit (<0.05 nM/min). (iii) S30 Table 1: TEG R and MA cells printed "UD" (undefined, R stated as >120 minutes) - where a cell is UD both with and without drug, no effect is measurable and the row says so rather than claiming a null. (iv) S29 Table 1: CADP-CT is 301 s for all five patients, an identical value consistent with a PFA-200 upper limit, though the source never states a ceiling - hedged, not asserted.

7. NOTHING WAS READ OFF A FIGURE IMAGE. Where a value exists only in a plotted panel the row carries readout_value NOT_REPORTED with readout_is_qualitative true and says which figure holds it. This applies to: the entire S27 anti-PEG aPTT titration (Figure 4b) and both murine carotid-flow experiments (Figure 5b, 5c); the S26 pre-drug aPTT baseline (Figure 3B); the S30 hemophilia B proteome panel (Figure 3C), the intermediate FXa isotherms (Figure 1A) and the TEG lysis curves (Figure 7). Numbers that the authors themselves wrote into the running text while citing a figure (for example S30's "from 270 nM with no aptamer to 380 nM") ARE extracted as numeric, because they are printed prose, and each such row names the figure the data are plotted in.

8. TWO ASSAY-INTERFERENCE HAZARDS THAT PROPAGATE BEYOND THIS BUNDLE. (i) S29 states the FVIII one-stage assay was deliberately run with a soy/rabbit-brain phosphatide, ellagic-acid activator "to avoid putative interference of PEG with silica-based clotting assays" - so for any PEGylated oligonucleotide a silica-activated aPTT or FVIII value may be a conjugate artefact rather than a pharmacological effect. Every PEGylated compound in this dataset needs an assay-reagent column. (ii) S31b PMID 21503856 and PMID 21724623 both derive "factor IX inhibition" from aPTT through a calibration curve rather than measuring factor activity; ">99% FIX inhibition" is a modelled quantity, and the rows say so.

9. PLATELET ROWS. Three rows use readout_category platelet_coag_crosstalk (S26 platelet count and its delta, S29 platelet count and ristocetin-induced aggregation). Each is included only because the source itself ties the platelet measurement to a coagulation-cascade readout in the same experiment - S26 states "we measured the ACT, aPTT, and platelet count of each animal over the course of the experiment"; S29 reports the platelet rise, the FVIII rise and the aPTT shortening as one mechanistically linked response to A1-domain blockade. Every one of these rows says in its notes that the primary home is the separate thrombocytopenia dossier. No platelet-only row was written.

10. ABSENCE ROWS ARE DISTINGUISHED FROM SILENCE THROUGHOUT. effect_direction "no_change" is used only where the source reports a measured null (S30 specificity controls, S30 whole-blood 5 pM TF failure, S30 alpha-TAT unchanged, S27 RB005 control, S26 circuit patency, S29 no serious/severe AEs, S31 no major bleeding, S31b PT nulls and repeat-dose reproducibility). Where the source simply never looked, effect_direction is NOT_REPORTED and the note names it as reporting silence - S26 bleeding (never assessed; the outcome set is coagulation assays, platelets, cytokines, blood gases, histopathology and echocardiography) and S29 thrombotic events (absent from the Table 2 adverse-event list, never declared an endpoint, and patients with previous thromboembolism were excluded).

11. A CLAIM IN THE TRIAGE SHEET THAT I COULD NOT SOURCE. The S30 triage note describes BAX499 as having "a documented clinical failure mode (paradoxical plasma TFPI rise, programme discontinued)". Neither the paradoxical TFPI rise nor the discontinuation appears anywhere in PMC3508133 or in any of the three BAX499 sibling abstracts. No row asserts it; it is recorded on the S30 oligo record as an explicitly unsourced claim so a curator does not later mistake it for extracted data.

12. TWO-SIDED LABEL SPACE, DELIBERATELY. Anticoagulant direction: S26 (ACT 96 -> 335 s, aPTT to 260 s), S27 (aPTT 30 -> 125 s), S31/S31b (aPTT 29.2 -> 52.2 s ladder, ACT 151 -> 236 s, mean aPTT 93.0 s). Procoagulant direction: S29 (aPTT 43 -> 31 s with FVIII 67% -> 134%) and S30/S31b BAX499 (peak thrombin 270 -> 380 nM, whole-blood clot time 8.3 -> 6.7 min in NORMAL blood). Reversal/antidote structure with baseline, on-drug and post-reversal values exists in S26, S31 and S31b PMID 20660806.

13. PARSING. All four PMC files are single-line JATS; line-based grep is unreliable on them and they were parsed with xml.etree. PMC6707742 and PMC3508133 have a <pmc-articleset> root, so the <article> child must be selected first - failing to do so silently yields only the floats-group and looks like a body-less record. Tables were recovered from <table-wrap>; in verbatim quotes of table rows the pipe separators are the parser's, and the cell values are verbatim. Entity references (P < .001) are resolved in quotes to the rendered text (P < .001).
refused_rows:
1. HEPARIN AND PROTAMINE COMPARATOR ARMS (S26). The heparin arm carries genuinely interesting coagulopathy numbers - ACT 389 ± 32 s, 349 ± 55 s, 320 ± 54 s, and an aPTT pinned at the 500 s assay ceiling. No rows were written for them because heparin and protamine are not oligonucleotides and every measurement row must hang off a local_oligo_key. The values are preserved in full inside the control_value and notes fields of the matched aptamer rows, including the ceiling annotation, so nothing is lost.

2. ANTI-PEG IMMUNOGENICITY MEASUREMENTS (S27). The paper's Figure 6 and Table 1 show that 6 of 18 healthy rhesus monkeys developed significant anti-PEG IgG after a SINGLE administration of RB006 (four exceeding 2 SD above the mean of pre-injection values), across IV and SC routes at 0.5, 1.0 and 1.5 mg/kg. This is a strong safety signal and it is the upstream cause of the S27 aPTT interference, but anti-PEG IgG titre is an immunogenicity readout, not a coagulation-cascade readout, and forcing it into readout_category would corrupt the endpoint definition. It is recorded on the S27_RB006 oligo record instead. The same applies to the ELISA and SPR binding data in Figures 1-3 (RUmax loss on FIXa binding), which are binding assays, not clotting assays.

3. NON-COAGULATION OUTCOMES IN S26. Mean arterial pressure (58 ± 6 vs 54 ± 3 mmHg at 30 min; 59 ± 8 vs 51 ± 5 mmHg at 3 h), echocardiographic shortening fraction (60 ± 16% vs 42 ± 8%, P = 0.01), the four interleukin/TNF-alpha time courses, blood gases, hematocrit and myocardial contraction band necrosis counts and areas are all quantified in Table 1, Table 2 and Figures 4-5. None is a coagulopathy readout. The shortening-fraction result is the paper's headline claim, and it is attributed to protamine's direct cardiodepressive effect rather than to anything coagulation-related, so importing it here would be miscategorisation. Not extracted.

4. S29 NON-COAGULATION AND SUPPLEMENT-ONLY DATA. Pharmacokinetics (Cmax 777 ng/mL, range 423-999; apparent half-life 5.84 days), VWF propeptide, VWF activity/antigen ratios, and the HMW/intermediate multimer patterns were left out: multimer normalisation is reported only as narrative and images (Figure 2 and supplemental Figure 1a) with no quantified multimer values in the retrieved text, and the healthy-volunteer platelet comparison sits in supplemental Figures 2-3 which were not retrieved. VWF propeptide is reported as "did not change (data not shown)" - a null with no inspectable data, so no absence row was written for it either. Non-bleeding adverse events in Table 2 (lymphadenopathy, tachycardia, diarrhoea, dyspepsia, nausea, urinary tract infection) are not coagulopathy events.

5. FIGURE-ONLY VALUES I DECLINED TO ESTIMATE. The S27 anti-PEG aPTT titration (Figure 4b) would yield the single most useful number in this bundle - the antibody:aptamer molar ratio at which the aptamer's anticoagulant effect is half lost - and the S27 murine carotid flow curves (Figure 5b-c) would yield percent-flow-versus-time. Both are plotted only. No value was estimated from either panel; those rows are qualitative with the direction and the p-value the text supplies. Likewise the S26 pre-drug aPTT baseline, the S30 hemophilia B proteome curves (Figure 3C) and the S30 TEG lysis traces (Figure 7).

6. "DATA NOT SHOWN" RESULTS WERE EXTRACTED ONLY AS FLAGGED ABSENCE ROWS, NEVER AS NUMBERS. S30 reports three such results: BAX499 had no effect on FXa without TFPI (data not shown); whole-blood thrombin generation at 5 pM TF was unimproved up to 1 uM (data not shown); and the TF titration that shifted clot times at <=1 pM (data not shown). Each is recorded as a qualitative null with "data not shown" stated in the notes, so a reviewer can see the evidence is not inspectable.

7. THE SECOND S26 REVERSAL VALUE WAS NOT SPLIT INTO TWO ROWS. Rather than write one ACT row and one aPTT row from a single ambiguous sentence - which would double-count a single measurement - one row was written with readout_name "ACT_or_aPTT_UNRESOLVED" and the conflict spelled out. A reviewer with the figure can resolve it; an extractor without it should not.

8. NO SEVERITY GRADE WAS ASSIGNED ANYWHERE. severity_stated_by_source carries only the source's own words ("Two moderate intensity bleeding events", "No major bleeding or other serious adverse events occurred", "There were no serious or severe adverse events", "One serious adverse event, an episode of transient encephalopathy"). Grading is left to the central rubric.

9. BAX499 PROGRAMME OUTCOME. I did not write a row, a max_phase value, or a discontinuation note asserting that the BAX499 programme failed or why, because no source in this bundle says so. See extraction_notes item 11.
